text:
Nora K: Quick check on the rollout timeline legend — the allocation bands are hard to read at a glance when small. PMs asked for a one-line way to read "10% -> canary" without opening the hover.
Diego: I noticed the same. On narrow widths the color ramp compresses and the 5/10/25 markers blur together. Could we add a thin divider line between major breakpoints?
Asha P: Divider lines help, but we should avoid relying on color alone. Propose adding a tiny icon (dot, dash) baked into the band when allocation < 20% so it's visible even if hue is similar.
Jonah: Be careful with adding icons — they add visual clutter in the mini-timeline. Maybe use icon only on focus/hover and use a thicker border on tiny bands.
ux-bot: automated-scan: low-contrast detected between band colors at 12% width, recommend contrast ratio >= 3:1 for stateful elements.
Nora K: Good call. Also, screen reader output for the timeline currently says "variant A: 10%". Can we change that to "variant A: currently receiving 10 percent of traffic (canary)" so it's clearer?
Asha P: Also want to standardize percent wording across the app: use "10 percent" not "10%" in aria labels. Keeps verbosity consistent.
Diego: On rollback flow copy: modal title is "Rollback deployment" and the primary is "Rollback". Suggest making title explicit: "Rollback deployment to version 2026-03-15" and primary "Confirm rollback — route new traffic to vX".
Jonah: UX note: when rolling back, we should show a compact timeline preview of the last 5 minutes allocations so users see immediate impact. Small sparkline under the confirm button maybe.
Nora K: Love the sparkline idea. Make sure it is live-updating only while modal is open and doesn't cause focus jumps.
Asha P: Keyboard accessibility: scrubber handle must expose aria-valuenow and aria-valuetext like "allocation 15 percent". Also ensure arrow keys nudge by 1% and shift+arrow by 5%.
Diego: For colorblind folks, let's switch categorical variants to Okabe-Ito base palette and then apply a separate sequential ramp for allocation intensity. That should keep variants distinct while preserving allocation meaning.
Jonah: Prototype two quick options in Figma: (1) border + subtle pattern for small bands, (2) hover-only icon + thicker borders. I'll attach links.
Nora K: Action list: Jonah uploads two comps, Asha updates aria copy and keyboard behavior docs, Diego files CSS fallback for borders, and I'll revise rollback modal copy. Back in 24h for review. :thumbsup:
